Ashara’s tail gives a small approving flick against her chair. “Useful distinction.”

Rashid inclines his head. “Fair correction. Rashid vel Amara, person.”

“I’m Thessaly Morrow,” says the fae woman. “Also a person. The sweet is mine.”

Seraphel takes the chair at your right.

“Seraphel Dawnquill,  
as established upstairs.  
And this is Ysolde Thornmantle.”

The white-haired woman looks from her untouched water to you. “Hello.”

“Caelindra Vaeyn,” says the elf, with the air of supplying an item that ought already to have been known.

At the head of the table, the angel rises just enough to make the gesture feel ceremonial. “Aldric Verantus. Welcome to Garvey House, Bing Bong.”

Servers begin setting down shallow bowls of squash soup, its surface bright with red oil and toasted seeds. Ashara waits until hers is in reach before picking up her spoon.

“You arrive on a good night,” she says. “No speeches from faculty. No seating chart beyond this one. We eat, and tomorrow they begin explaining what they expect us to become.”

Rashid glances toward the place card bearing your family name.

“And tonight,” he says, “we get to hear what brought the first human Conclave student in sixty years to our table.”
